discovery: Experimental discovery of the fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect (zero-field fractional Chern insulators) in moire materials
subfield: Condensed matter physics - topological quantum matter
motivation: For four decades fractionally charged anyons were thought to require strong magnetic fields and Landau levels. Theory predicted that interacting electrons in topological flat bands could form fractional Chern insulators spontaneously, with no external field. In 2023-2024 Xiaodong Xu's group, through optical and transport measurements on twisted MoTe2, and Tingxin Li's group, through transport, observed quantized fractional Hall plateaus at zero magnetic field. Long Ju's group independently found the same fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene on hBN. These experiments turn an abstract idea, fractionalization driven by band topology and interactions alone, into a real and tunable materials platform. They have opened a field: zero-field anyons, possible non-Abelian states and new routes to topological quantum computation, and many groups are now building on them. This is a clean, conceptually deep discovery in which theory and experiment met.
